newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Child among eight killed in new Karachi violence.
newsitem.headline: Child among eight killed in new Karachi violence.

text.p: Eight people, including a four-year-old boy, were killed in various incidents of violence in Pakistan's volatile city of Karachi on Wednesday, police said.
Violence has surged in this southern port in recent weeks on renewed tension between the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and the breakaway MQM-Haqiqi faction.

Witnesses said shopping centres and state-owned banks in District South were closed for a second day in a strike enforced by ethnic party militants after nine people, including five MQM activists, were killed on Monday.
Police said a man slit the throat of a four-year-old boy, identified only as Arman, in Orangi Town on Wednesday.
They said the bodies of two men, with their hands tied and who had been shot, were found in jute sacks in the boot of a car near Karimabad Bridge in District Central.
A third man was shot dead in eastern district's Zaman Town and another man was killed in a drive-by shooting in Gulshan-i-Iqbal in the same district.
The bullet-riddled bodies of two middle-aged men were found in different areas of the western district of Orangi. Police said both the men were reported missing a day earlier.
Gunmen killed a journalist and wounded an ethnic party leader in the early hours of Wednesday.

Police said unidentified assailants fired on Kamran Rizvi, an MQM-Haqiqi leader as he stepped out of his house in District Central to see off a visiting friend, Manzar Imkani, a senior sub-editor at the Urdu-language Jang newspaper.
Imkani, 49, died instantly while Rizvi, 35, was seriously wounded. Neighbours took him to hospital.
A Haqiqi spokesman accused the mainstream MQM of carrying out the attack. MQM officials denied responsibility.

"We have been warned to keep shops shut on Thursday also," said a shopkeeper in Frere Road. Unidentified activists on motorcycles had told them they could reopen for business after prayers had been offered on Thursday for the five slain MQM activists, he added.
The mainstream MQM's London-based leader Altaf Hussain ordered the closure of more than 100 party offices in Karachi after Monday's deadly attack on an MQM branch.
More than 85 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian unrest in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.

The MQM, long involved in a struggle with the security forces as well as with MQM-Haqiqi, was brought into a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, after national and provincial elections on February 3.
